title: Bisphenol A (BPA) degradation by Microbial Fuel Cells bioanodes and by microbial isolates from activated sludge
description: We investigated the microbial populations at the anode of Microbial Fuel Cells (MFCs) using synthetic wastewater as anolyte, in presence and absence of bisphenol A (BPA). All systems were inoculated with activated sludge from a municipal wastewater treatment plant and fed with sodium acetate as main source of carbon and energy to sustain microbial metabolism at the anode. All MFCs used the same layout: two-chambers separated by a cationic exchange membrane, aerated PBS and carbon cloth, abiotic cathode.We used a Next Generation Sequencing method (ILLUMINA) to screen the rRNA 16S of both Eubacteria and Archaebacteria in biofilms. We used the data obtained to estimate the alfa- and beta-biodiversity of MFC_BPA and MFC_no_BPA bioanodes through the Shannon, the Simpson and the Bray-Curtis indexes.We also investigated the ability of microbial isolate (from the same environmental source) to grow using BPA as sole source of carbon. and their phenotype through Biolog Ecoplates.This bioproject includes metagenomes from the bioanode of MFCs operating in presence and in absence of BPA and the results of the 16S rRNA sequencing of two isolates, that dimonstrated the highest BPA removal rate in mineral media.
